instructions: Stand with a dumbbell at each side and palms facing inward.
Keep the upper arms beside your torso and curl one weight toward its shoulder.
Lower it with control as you begin curling the other arm.
Continue alternating without rotating the palms forward or swinging your torso.
Recline on an incline bench with feet planted and a dumbbell hanging at each side.
Turn the palms forward and keep the upper arms beside your torso, clear of the bench.
Curl one weight toward its shoulder without moving the upper arm.
Lower slowly, then curl the other weight.
Continue alternating while keeping your back supported.
Stand upright holding dumbbells in front of your thighs with palms facing backward.
Keep a slight elbow bend and raise one weight forward to shoulder height, palm down.
Lower it slowly without leaning back.
Repeat with the other arm and continue alternating.
Lie back on an incline bench with feet planted and a dumbbell beside each shoulder.
Press one dumbbell upward while the other remains near your chest.
Lower the raised weight with control, then press with the opposite arm.
Continue alternating while keeping your back on the bench.
Adjust the seat and sit with your back supported, placing one foot on each platform.
Hold the handles and keep both feet centered on their platforms.
Press one platform away until that leg is nearly straight.
Bend the knee slowly to return, then press with the other leg.
Continue alternating while keeping your pelvis against the seat.
Adjust the seat so your chest rests against the pad and both feet are supported.
Hold the close handles with palms facing each other.
Pull one handle toward your ribs, keeping the elbow close to your torso.
Return it slowly while keeping your chest on the pad.
Repeat with the other arm and continue alternating.
Stand with feet planted and dumbbells in front of your shoulders, palms facing each other and elbows pointing forward.
Press one dumbbell overhead while keeping your torso upright.
Lower it to shoulder height, then press with the other arm.
Continue alternating without leaning backward.
Place two stable kettlebells on the floor and grip the handles in a high plank.
Set your feet wide enough to keep your hips steady.
Pull one kettlebell toward your lower ribs with the elbow close to your side.
Return it firmly to the floor under control.
Keep your chest and pelvis facing the floor, finish the repetitions and change arms.
Sit upright with your feet on the supports and take the handles beside your head.
Keep the moving pads in firm contact with your upper body as you hold the handles.
Gently tighten your abdomen and curl your chest toward your pelvis without pulling with your arms.
Return slowly to the upright starting position without reclining far backward.
Sit with your back supported and feet planted, holding dumbbells in front of your shoulders with palms toward you.
Move your elbows outward as you begin pressing upward.
Continue overhead, turning your palms forward as your arms extend.
Lower along the same path, bringing your elbows forward and palms toward you again.
Lie on your back on a flat bench with feet planted and a dumbbell in each hand.
Start with the weights near your hips and a slight bend in your elbows.
Sweep both arms outward and around toward the space behind your head, keeping the elbow bend steady.
Reverse the arc to bring the dumbbells back toward your hips.
Use a controlled range that keeps your shoulders comfortable and your back supported.
Stand facing the back of a stable incline bench and hold the top of its backrest with both hands.
Bend your hips and knees to lower into a squat.
Keep your feet flat and use the support to steady your balance.
Push through both feet to stand while keeping your grip light.
Fix the band at chest height and stand facing the anchor.
Hold a handle in each hand with your arms extended forward and elbows softly bent.
Open your arms out to the sides while drawing your shoulder blades together.
Return your hands forward slowly without shrugging or leaning back.
Secure the assistance band to the pull-up bar and position its lower loop beneath your lower thighs.
Grip the bar with your palms facing away from you and lift your feet clear of the floor.
Pull your elbows down to bring your chin toward bar height without swinging.
Lower slowly until your arms extend while the band continues to support your legs.
Attach the bands to a low anchor beyond your feet and secure the foot attachments.
Lie on your back with your fingertips behind your head and lift your shoulders slightly.
Bend one knee toward your chest while turning the opposite shoulder toward it and extending the other leg.
Switch the leg and shoulder positions in a controlled pedaling motion.
Keep your lower back steady and avoid pulling on your neck.
Stand on the middle of the band and hold one handle in each hand in front of your thighs.
Keep your palms facing your thighs and your elbows slightly bent.
Raise both arms forward toward shoulder height without swinging your body.
Lower your hands slowly to your thighs.
Anchor a band to one side at about chest height and stand sideways to it with your feet apart.
Hold the band with both hands in front of your chest and gently tighten your abdomen.
Press your hands upward until your arms are overhead, keeping your hips and chest facing forward.
Bring your hands back to your chest with control.
Complete all reps facing one direction, then turn to face the other way.
Anchor the band at chest height and stand sideways to it with your feet apart.
Hold the handle in both hands at the middle of your chest and step far enough away to create tension.
Tighten your abdomen and press your hands straight forward without turning toward the anchor.
Pause briefly, then bring your hands back to your chest under control.
Complete all reps on one side, then switch.
Secure the band to a low anchor and stand facing away from it.
Reach between your legs and hold the band with both hands, then step forward to create tension.
With soft knees, push your hips back and let your hands travel between your thighs.
Press through your feet and straighten your hips to stand tall.
Push your hips backward again slowly without rounding your back or leaning backward at the top.
Anchor a band high in front of you and hold a handle in each hand.
Stand tall with your arms reaching forward and upward toward the anchor.
Pull your elbows out and back, bringing the handles toward your upper chest without shrugging.
Reach toward the anchor again with control.
Stand on the middle of a resistance band with your feet about hip-width apart.
Hold the ends at your sides with your arms straight.
Lift your shoulders toward your ears without bending your elbows or rolling the shoulders.
Lower your shoulders slowly.
Anchor a band in front of you around chest height and hold a handle in each hand.
Step back until the band is taut, then squat with your arms reaching toward the anchor.
Stand up and pull the handles toward the sides of your ribs, drawing your elbows back.
Extend your arms toward the anchor as you lower into the next squat.
Stand on the middle of a band and hold a handle in each hand beside your legs.
Keep a small, steady bend in your knees and lower your torso forward, letting your hands travel down close to your legs.
Lower only as far as you can control without bouncing or pulling yourself deeper.
Drive your hips forward and raise your torso to standing, keeping your arms long.
Anchor a band low beyond your feet and fasten it securely around both ankles.
Lie on your back with your legs extended and your arms reaching overhead.
Raise your legs and upper body together, reaching your hands toward your feet as you balance on your hips.
Lower your torso, arms and legs slowly toward the starting position.
Secure the band low in front of you and hold a handle in each hand with your arms down.
Stand tall with your knees relaxed and your abdomen gently tightened.
Keep a slight bend in your elbows and raise your arms forward and outward into a Y shape overhead.
Lower your hands slowly toward your thighs without leaning your torso backward.
Place a loop band around your ankles and stand with your feet apart.
Bend your knees and hips slightly into an athletic stance.
Step sideways with one foot, then bring the other foot after it without allowing the band to go slack.
Keep your knees pointing with your toes and your hips at a steady height.
Continue for several steps, then reverse direction.
Hang from a fixed horizontal bar with your palms facing away from you.
Use a coordinated pull and controlled body swing to bring your chest high toward the bar.
Move your shoulders and wrists over the bar as your elbows turn behind you.
Press down on the bar to straighten your arms above it.
Bend your arms and lower through the transition to a controlled hang.
Kneel on the floor and grip a barbell fitted with round plates that can roll freely.
Place the bar under your shoulders and gently tighten your abdomen.
Roll it forward, letting your hips and arms extend only as far as you can prevent your lower back from sagging.
Pull the bar back toward your knees while keeping your torso controlled.
Lie on a flat bench beneath the racked bar with your feet firmly on the floor.
Grip the bar with your palms facing away from you and your hands slightly wider than your shoulders.
Lift it clear of the rack and steady it above your chest with your shoulder blades supported on the bench.
Bend your elbows to lower the bar toward your chest without bouncing it.
Press the bar upward until your arms are straight, then return it securely to the rack when finished.
Stand tall holding a barbell with your palms facing forward and your hands about shoulder-width apart.
Keep your upper arms close to your sides and let the bar hang in front of your thighs.
Curl the bar toward your shoulders without swinging your body or moving your elbows far forward.
Lower it slowly until your arms are nearly straight.
Stand close to the bar with your feet about hip-width apart and the bar over the middle of your feet.
Bend your hips and knees and grip the bar just outside your legs with your arms straight.
Tighten your abdomen and push through the floor, raising your hips and shoulders together while keeping the bar close.
Stand tall without leaning backward, then push your hips back and bend your knees to lower the bar to the floor.
Stand holding a barbell in front of your thighs with your palms facing your body.
Keep a small, fixed bend in your elbows and gently tighten your abdomen.
Raise the bar forward until your arms reach about shoulder height without swinging or leaning back.
Lower the bar slowly to your thighs.
Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
Position a light barbell securely across your hip crease before placing your hands on the floor beside you. Keep your hands on the bar instead if it will not stay stable.
Gently tighten your abdomen and press through your feet to lift your hips until your torso and thighs form a line.
Lower your hips under control without overextending your lower back.
Stand just in front of a barbell on the floor with your feet about hip-width apart.
Bend your knees and hips to grip the bar behind your legs with your arms straight.
Push through your feet to stand, letting the bar travel close behind your calves and thighs.
Bend your knees and hips to lower the bar back toward the floor without rounding forward.
Sit in front of a stable flat bench with your upper back against its edge and your knees bent.
Position a barbell across your hip crease and hold it steady with both hands.
Keep your feet flat and press through them to lift your hips until your torso and thighs form a line, with your upper back supported on the bench.
Lower your hips slowly in front of the bench without sliding your shoulders off it.
Lie back on an incline bench beneath the rack with your feet planted.
Grip the bar slightly wider than your shoulders with your palms facing away.
Unrack it and lower it toward your upper chest, keeping your shoulder blades supported.
Press upward until your arms are straight, then rack the bar after the set.
Hold a barbell across your upper back and stand tall with your feet about hip-width apart.
Take a controlled step forward and bend both knees, lowering the back knee toward the floor.
Keep the front foot planted and your torso steady as you lower.
Push through the front foot to return to the start. Complete the set with the same leg, then switch legs.
Hold a barbell with a palms-back grip wider than shoulder width.
Bend your knees slightly, push your hips back and lean forward until your torso is nearly horizontal.
Pull the bar toward your upper chest while lifting your elbows out to the sides.
Lower the bar under control without changing your torso angle.
Stand on the floor with a barbell across your upper back and your feet about hip-width apart.
Step one foot backward and land on the ball of that foot.
Bend both knees to lower your back knee toward the floor, keeping your front foot flat and your torso upright.
Push through your front foot to return to standing.
Complete all reps on one side, then switch.
Kneel near the end of a stable flat bench with a barbell and round plates on the floor in front of it.
Grip the bar with both hands and hold your abdomen firm.
Roll the bar forward along the floor as your body lengthens from your knees, stopping before your lower back sags.
Draw the bar back toward the bench with control.
Sit on a flat bench with your feet apart and firmly on the floor.
Hold the bar at the front of your shoulders with a palms-forward grip just wider than shoulder width.
Press it overhead while keeping your abdomen firm and avoiding a backward lean.
Lower it slowly to the front of your shoulders.
Stand holding a barbell in front of your thighs with your palms facing back.
Keep your elbows straight and your torso upright.
Lift your shoulders toward your ears without rolling them or bending your arms.
Lower your shoulders slowly.
Stand with your feet apart and rest a light barbell across your upper back, holding it with both hands.
Keep your hips facing forward and knees relaxed.
Bend your torso to one side through a comfortable range without turning your chest.
Return upright under control. Complete the repetitions, then repeat on the other side.
Stand in a wide stance with a barbell across your upper back and both feet planted.
Shift your hips toward one side and bend that knee, keeping the other leg straight.
Lower through a controlled range with the bar level and your chest lifted.
Push through the bent leg to return to the upright wide stance.
Complete all reps on one side, then switch.
Stand holding a barbell in front of your thighs and shift your weight onto one foot.
Keep a small bend in that knee and lift the other foot clear of the floor.
Push your hips back as your torso lowers and your free leg reaches behind you, keeping the bar close to the standing leg.
Return to standing with control.
Complete all reps on one side, then switch.
Set the bar on the muscular upper back just below your neck and grip it firmly.
Stand with your feet about shoulder-width apart.
Lower into a squat while keeping your chest lifted, heels down and knees aligned with your feet.
Press through both feet to stand.
Position a stable flat bench behind you and hold the bar across your upper back, below the neck.
Grip the bar firmly and stand in front of the bench.
Bend your hips and knees to sit lightly on the bench with your feet planted.
Gently tighten your abdomen and press through both feet to stand without rocking.
Take a barbell across your upper back and step onto a stable low platform with your forefeet supported and heels free.
Stand tall with your knees nearly straight.
Raise your heels by pressing through the balls of your feet.
Lower the heels slowly below the step edge within a comfortable range.
Sit at the edge of a stable flat bench and grip the edge beside your hips.
Move your hips just in front of the bench and extend your legs with your heels on the floor.
Bend your elbows to lower your body close to the bench through a comfortable range.
Straighten your arms to raise your hips again without changing your foot position.
Secure the band beneath a stable flat bench so both ends rise beside your chest.
Lie on the bench with your feet planted and hold one handle in each hand.
Press both hands upward over your chest until your arms extend.
Lower your hands slowly to chest level while keeping your wrists aligned with your forearms.
Place one forearm across a stable flat bench with the elbow below your shoulder.
Extend both legs to the side and stack your feet on the floor.
Lift your hips so your shoulders, hips and feet form a straight line and hold while breathing normally.
Lower with control and repeat on the other side.
Lie on a flat bench with your knees bent and both feet resting on the bench.
Hold a barbell above your chest with your palms facing away and a small bend in the elbows.
Keep that elbow angle as you lower the bar behind your head within a comfortable range.
Bring the bar back above your chest without lifting your ribs or hips from the bench.
Sit on the edge of a stable flat bench with your hands beside your hips.
Slide your hips just off the edge, keeping your knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
Bend your elbows to lower your hips through a comfortable range close to the bench.
Press through your palms to straighten your arms and rise.
Lie on your back with your arms extended out to the sides.
Lift both feet and bend your hips and knees so your knees are above your hips.
Keep your knees together as you lower both legs toward one side through a comfortable range.
Bring the knees back through the center and lower them toward the other side without forcing floor contact.
Hold a barbell with a palms-back grip just wider than your shoulders.
Bend your knees slightly, push your hips backward and lean forward while keeping your back shape steady.
Pull the bar toward your upper abdomen by driving your elbows behind you.
Lower the bar until your arms are straight while keeping the same torso angle.
Stand between two low pulleys and hold the opposite-side handle in each hand.
Bend your knees slightly, push your hips back and lean forward, letting your arms hang beneath your shoulders.
Keep a small steady bend in your elbows as you raise both arms outward to about torso level.
Lower the handles slowly beneath your chest without lifting your torso.
Stand with knees slightly bent and hinge forward, keeping your back steady.
Let the dumbbells hang beneath your shoulders with palms facing each other.
Keep a small elbow bend and lift both arms out to the sides.
Lower slowly without raising your torso.
Set an incline bench at a height that lets you hinge forward and rest your forehead lightly against its padded top.
Plant your feet, bend your knees slightly, and hold the dumbbells below your shoulders.
Keep a small elbow bend and lift your arms out to the sides without pressing heavily through your head.
Lower the weights slowly while keeping your torso steady.
Face a low pulley with one foot forward and hold its handle in the opposite hand.
Push your hips back and lean forward, resting your free hand on your front thigh.
Pull the handle toward your lower ribs with your elbow close to your side and your torso steady.
Extend your working arm slowly.
Complete all reps on one side, then switch.
Stand holding a dumbbell in each hand with palms toward your body.
Bend your knees slightly and hinge at your hips until your torso leans forward.
Let the weights hang below your shoulders, keeping your back steady.
Pull your elbows back to bring the dumbbells toward the sides of your lower chest.
Lower slowly until your arms extend without rounding your back.
Stand upright with your hands on your hips.
Step forward with one foot and bend both knees to lower your body.
Keep your front foot planted and your front knee tracking with your toes.
Push through the front foot to return to standing.
Repeat with the other leg and continue alternating.
Set a split stance with one foot forward and one behind, keeping enough sideways space to balance.
Keep both feet in place as you bend the knees and lower your rear knee toward the floor.
Maintain a controlled torso and keep the front heel planted.
Push through your front foot to return to the top of the split stance.
Repeat, then change which foot is forward.
Stand with your feet about shoulder-width apart.
Raise your arms to shoulder height.
Bend your hips and knees to sit down, reaching your arms forward for balance.
Keep your heels down, chest up and knees in line with your toes.
Press through your feet to stand back up.
Stand with the balls of both feet on a sturdy step and your heels beyond its edge.
Use a railing or wall for balance if needed.
Keep your knees nearly straight and lift your heels through a controlled range.
Lower your heels slowly below the edge, then repeat.
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Take a step forward with your right leg, lowering your body into a lunge position.
Keep your torso controlled and guide the front knee in the same direction as your toes.
Push off with your right foot and bring your left foot forward, stepping into a lunge position with your left leg.
Continue alternating legs and walking forward, maintaining a controlled and steady pace.
Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat, about hip-width apart.
Place your arms beside you and gently tighten your abdomen.
Press through your feet and lift your hips until your trunk and thighs form a line.
Lower your hips to the floor with control, keeping your knees aligned with your feet.
Lie on your back with the soles of your feet together and knees open to the sides.
Cross your arms over your chest.
Curl your shoulders and upper back off the floor without moving your feet.
Lower slowly until your upper back rests on the floor again.
Stand facing away from a low pulley and hold its bar in front of your thighs with your palms facing back.
Keep your feet planted and elbows nearly straight.
Raise the bar forward to shoulder height without leaning backward.
Lower it slowly along the same arc.
Sit at a cable chest press station with your back against the pad and your feet on the floor.
Hold a handle in each hand beside your chest, with your elbows bent and pointing out and slightly down.
Keep your back against the pad and press both handles forward until your arms are nearly straight.
Bend your elbows slowly to return the handles beside your chest.
Keep your wrists straight and control the return before pressing again.
Set both cable pulleys above shoulder height and hold a handle in each hand.
Stand between the pulleys with your feet apart and lean forward slightly from your hips.
Open your arms upward and out to the sides with a small bend in your elbows.
Bring your arms down and forward in an arc until your hands meet in front of your hips.
Reverse the arc slowly, keeping the same elbow bend and avoiding a backward swing of your torso.
Attach a rope to a high pulley and kneel facing the machine.
Hold the rope ends beside your head and keep both knees planted.
Curl your rib cage toward your pelvis, bringing your elbows downward without pulling mainly with your arms.
Uncurl slowly to the starting position while keeping the rope at your head.
Stand between two low cable pulleys with a handle in each hand at your sides.
Bend your hips and knees to lower while keeping your arms straight and chest lifted.
Push through both feet to extend your knees and hips until you stand upright.
Lower again with control, keeping the handles close to your sides.
Stand facing a low pulley and take a palms-up grip on its straight bar.
Begin with your arms extended and the bar close to your thighs.
Bend your elbows and draw them backward as you slide the bar upward close to your torso.
Lower the bar slowly while allowing the elbows to return beside your body.
Place a flat bench between two low cable pulleys and hold one handle in each hand.
Lie back with your feet planted and bring the handles beside your chest with elbows bent.
Press both handles above your chest until your arms are straight.
Lower the handles slowly to chest level while keeping your back and hips supported.
Attach a rope to a low cable pulley and stand facing it.
Hold one rope end in each hand with your palms facing each other and arms extended.
Bend your elbows to curl the rope upward without moving your upper arms forward.
Lower slowly until your elbows are nearly straight.
Attach an ankle strap to a low pulley and stand sideways with your working leg closest to the machine.
Hold the machine lightly for balance and lift your strapped foot clear of the floor.
Keep your working knee nearly straight as you draw that leg inward across the front of your standing leg.
Return slowly outward.
Complete all reps on one side, then switch.
Place an incline bench between two low cable pulleys and hold one handle in each hand.
Recline against the bench with your feet planted and handles beside your upper chest.
Press upward and inward until your arms are straight above your chest.
Lower slowly while keeping your back and hips against the bench.
Place an incline bench facing away from a low cable pulley with a bar attached.
Recline with your feet planted and hold the bar above your head using a comfortable two-hand grip.
Keep your upper arms steady as you bend your elbows to lower the bar behind your head.
Straighten your elbows to raise the bar again without lifting your back from the pad.
Sit on the floor beside a cable pulley set near elbow height, with your legs extended, and hold the handle in the hand nearest it.
Bend that elbow to a right angle and keep it tucked beside your waist, with your forearm pointing toward the cable.
Rotate at the shoulder to bring your hand across the front of your abdomen, keeping your elbow in place.
Return your forearm slowly toward the pulley without turning your torso.
Complete all reps on one side, then switch.
Attach a straight bar to a high pulley. Stand facing it with your feet apart and hold the bar with both hands.
Reach the bar forward and upward with your elbows slightly bent.
Pull the bar down toward one hip while turning your shoulders slightly toward that side.
Return the bar slowly to the raised position.
Sweep the bar toward the other hip, then continue alternating sides with your feet planted.
Attach a single handle to a high pulley and stand facing the cable.
Hold the handle in one hand with your palm facing up, elbow bent and tucked beside your ribs.
Straighten your elbow to move the handle downward toward your thigh without moving your upper arm forward or back.
Let your elbow bend slowly as the handle rises to the starting position.
Keep your wrist steady, finish the repetitions, and switch arms.
Sit at a preacher bench facing a low cable pulley and rest your upper arms on the pad.
Hold the cable bar with palms facing upward and begin with elbows nearly straight.
Curl the bar toward your shoulders while keeping your upper arms on the pad.
Lower the bar slowly without forcing the elbows straight.
Stand facing two high cable pulleys. Hold the left handle in your right hand and the right handle in your left so the cables cross.
Reach your hands forward at about shoulder height with a slight bend in your elbows.
Pull your arms out to the sides and slightly down, bringing your shoulder blades toward each other.
Stop when your arms are roughly in line with your torso.
Return slowly to the crossed position without changing your elbow bend.
Secure the low cable attachment around your feet and lie on your back with your feet toward the pulley.
Place your hands on the floor beside you and bend your hips and knees so your legs are raised.
Curl your pelvis upward to bring your bent knees toward your chest, keeping your upper back on the floor.
Lower your pelvis slowly and return the legs to the starting position without letting the cable pull you abruptly.
Attach a rope to a low pulley and stand facing away from it.
Hold one rope end in each hand behind your head, with your elbows pointing upward.
Gently tighten your abdomen and straighten your elbows to raise your hands overhead.
Bend the elbows slowly to lower the rope behind your head without leaning backward.
Position a stability ball beside a high cable pulley. Hold the handle with both hands and carefully lower your upper back onto the ball.
Plant your feet apart on the floor, bend your knees, and lift your hips so your trunk is supported between your shoulders and feet.
Extend your arms above your chest with a slight bend in your elbows.
Turn your shoulders and arms away from the pulley, keeping your hips steady and your feet planted.
Return slowly toward the pulley without letting the cable pull you off balance.
After completing one side, reposition the ball and repeat facing the other direction.
Place a flat bench in front of a high pulley with a rope attached. Sit facing away from the pulley with your feet planted.
Hold the rope ends beside your head and keep your hips on the bench.
Gently tighten your abdomen, then curl your upper body forward to bring your chest toward your thighs.
Keep your hands beside your head instead of pulling the rope down with your arms.
Raise your chest slowly to the starting position without leaning backward.
Place a flat bench between two low cable pulleys. Sit with your feet planted and hold the opposite cable handle in each hand.
Lean forward from your hips until your chest is close to your thighs. Let your hands hang below your shoulders.
With a slight bend in your elbows, open your arms out to the sides until they are roughly in line with your shoulders.
Lower the handles slowly beneath your chest.
Keep the forward lean and elbow bend steady throughout the movement.
Stand between two low cable pulleys and hold a handle in each hand.
Bring the handles beside your shoulders with your elbows bent and pointing out. Plant your feet about hip-width apart.
Gently tighten your abdomen and press both handles overhead until your arms are nearly straight.
Lower the handles slowly to shoulder height.
Keep your torso upright and avoid leaning backward as you press.
Attach a short bar to a low pulley and stand facing it with your feet about hip-width apart.
Hold the bar in front of your thighs with your palms facing your body and your arms straight.
Raise your shoulders toward your ears without bending your elbows or rolling your shoulders.
Lower your shoulders slowly and let them settle before repeating.
Stand sideways beside a low cable pulley. Hold the handle in the hand nearest the pulley and let that arm hang beside your thigh.
Plant your feet about shoulder-width apart and keep your chest facing forward.
Bend sideways away from the pulley, moving your ribs toward the opposite hip without turning your torso.
Return slowly toward the pulley through a comfortable range.
Finish the repetitions, then turn around and repeat on the other side.
Attach a short bar to a low pulley and sit on a flat bench facing the cable.
Hold the bar with your palms facing up. Lean forward and rest your forearms on your thighs with your wrists just beyond your knees.
Keep your forearms supported and bend your wrists to raise the bar toward you.
Lower the bar slowly by letting your wrists extend through a comfortable range.
Keep a secure grip and avoid lifting your elbows from your thighs.
Sit against the backrest and place the balls of your feet on the footplate with your heels free to move.
Set the seat distance so your knees stay slightly bent, then hold the side handles.
Push through the balls of your feet to point your toes away and move the footplate.
Let your ankles bend back slowly while keeping the knee angle nearly unchanged.
Stand on the middle of a band with your feet about hip-width apart.
Hold the band ends at your sides with your arms straight and your body tall.
Keep your knees nearly straight and raise both heels as high as you can control.
Lower your heels slowly to the floor.
Set two cable pulleys around chest height and stand between them with one foot forward.
Hold a handle in each hand with arms open and elbows slightly bent.
Sweep both handles together in front of your chest without changing the elbow bend.
Open your arms slowly back to the starting position.
Lie face down along an incline bench with your chest against the pad and your feet braced on the floor.
Hold a barbell below you with your palms facing back and arms extended.
Pull the bar toward your lower chest, driving your elbows back while keeping your chest on the pad.
Lower the bar slowly until your arms extend again.
Place an incline bench facing the pulley and sit with your chest against the angled pad and feet planted.
Grip the bar with both palms down and extend your arms toward the cable.
Pull the bar toward your lower chest, moving your elbows backward close to your sides.
Extend your arms slowly while maintaining chest contact with the pad.
Lie face down against an incline bench with your feet braced on the floor.
Hold the bar below your shoulders using an underhand grip with your palms facing forward.
Keep your chest on the pad and draw your elbows back to pull the bar toward your upper abdomen.
Lower slowly until your arms are straight again.
Start in a push-up position with your hands slightly wider than your shoulders and your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Bend your elbows to lower your chest toward the floor.
Press forcefully through both hands so they leave the floor together.
Briefly bring both hands to your chest, then return them beneath your shoulders before landing.
Land with your elbows slightly bent to absorb the impact and regain control before the next repetition.
Grip a secure overhead bar with your palms facing you and your hands about shoulder-width apart.
Let your body hang with your arms extended and your feet off the floor.
Pull your elbows down toward your sides to raise your chest toward the bar until your chin clears it.
Lower yourself slowly until your arms are extended again.
Keep your body steady and avoid swinging your legs to start the next pull.
Lie on a flat bench with your feet planted and take a palms-away grip around shoulder width or slightly narrower.
Unrack the bar and hold it above your chest with your wrists stacked over your forearms.
Lower it toward your chest, keeping your elbows closer to your sides than in a wide-grip press.
Press the bar back up without bouncing, then return it to the rack after the set.
Lie on your back on a flat bench with feet planted and a dumbbell in each hand.
Hold the weights close together above your chest, palms facing each other.
Bend your elbows to lower the weights toward your chest, keeping your upper arms close to your torso.
Press both dumbbells upward until your arms are extended.
Lower with control without bouncing the weights against your body.
Stand upright holding the inner angled grips of an EZ bar with palms up.
Keep the upper arms beside your torso and curl the bar toward your shoulders.
Pause briefly without leaning backward.
Lower slowly until the elbows are extended.
Place your hands close together beneath your chest and rest both knees on the floor behind you.
Move your knees back enough to form a straight line from your head through your hips to your knees.
Bend your elbows back beside your ribs and lower your chest toward your hands.
